p3_b0.ocr: The first table presents data on the formulation effects, with headers including Formulation, GI, % Change from white bread control, and P Value. The Control group has a GI of 59.3 ± 24.7, with no change or P Value indicated. The 1500 mg Capsule exhibits a GI of 61.9 ± 2.6, a % Change from white bread control of -4.39, and a P Value of 0.77. The 2000 mg Capsule shows a GI of 45.1 ± 14.2, a % Change of 24.01, and a P Value of 0.076. The 3000 mg Capsule has a GI of 46.8 ± 12.5, with a % Change of 21.05 and a P Value of 0.11.

p3_b1.ocr: The 1500 mg Powder has a GI of 43.6 ± 15.7, a % Change of 26.41, and a P Value of 0.11. The 2000 mg Powder presents a GI of 45.2 ± 14.1, with a % Change of 23.76 and a P Value of 0.16. Finally, the 3000 mg Powder has a GI of 39.1 ± 20.2, a % Change of 34.11, and a P Value of 0.023. The second table details regulators with headers as Name of regulator, Peptide, Group, and Role of mechanism, where Rgg corresponds to SHP, ComS (XIP), classified under Streptococci for Commensalism/Virulence; NprR associates with NprX in Bacilli for Necrotrophism; PlcR with PapR in Bacilli for Virulence; PrgX, TraA with cCF10 iCF10 in Enterococci for Virulence; and TprA with PhrA in Streptococci for Commensalism.
